biological_hypothesis: Cooler warm-season climates favour visible anthocyanin-associated colour through plastic regulation, evolved differentiation, or thermal/optical functions.
evidence: Direct floral studies show increased anthocyanin at cooler temperatures; Campanula americana floral reflectance covaries with temperature.
limitations: Long-term climatic geography, not temperature during corolla development; CIELAB a* is not an anthocyanin assay.

candidate: Temperature seasonality (BIO4) and Temperature PC1 x seasonality
biological_hypothesis: The flower-colour response to mean warm-season temperature can depend on recurrent annual thermal variation.
evidence: Floral anthocyanin production is temperature-sensitive and genotype-dependent; current exact INLA screen supports the interaction for conditional intensity.
limitations: BIO4 is an annual variability proxy, not direct frost or pre-anthesis temperature exposure.

candidate: BIO6 minimum temperature of coldest month
biological_hypothesis: Winter/cold-extreme geography may mark dormancy, germination history, or regional lineages, but is less directly tied to summer corolla development.
evidence: Campanula punctata shows geographical variation in thermal germination responses; floral anthocyanin responds to cool temperatures in other taxa.
limitations: Highly collinear with mean climate and biologically mismatched to flowering season.

biological_hypothesis: Drier climates can increase the protective value or regulation of anthocyanin-associated pigmentation.
public_proxy: CHELSA CMI, annual precipitation, driest-month precipitation
evidence: Across floral polymorphisms pigmentation is positively associated with aridity/VPD; drought can deepen petal anthocyanin in experimental systems.
limitations: Supply-side climatic proxy; not flower-level water status or atmospheric demand.

biological_hypothesis: Atmospheric drying demand may be more physiologically informative than precipitation alone for drought-associated floral pigmentation.
evidence: Floral anthocyanin frequency has been positively associated with VPD across taxa.
limitations: Long-term mean VPD, not observation-year or flower-development VPD.

biological_hypothesis: Integrated precipitation-demand balance may capture effective water limitation missed by rainfall summaries.
evidence: Anthocyanin stress responses are linked to drought; CHELSA provides an explicit water-balance metric.
limitations: Climatic balance, not measured soil moisture; may overlap CMI and VPD.

biological_hypothesis: The biological meaning of mean moisture may differ where water supply is intermittent.
evidence: Drought responses motivate a variability sensitivity; prior interaction screen did not support a standalone promotion.
limitations: Annual coefficient of variation, not event timing during flowering.

biological_hypothesis: Extreme wet-season climate may distinguish oceanic/snowy regions but has no strong direct floral-anthocyanin prediction.
evidence: Completeness guardrail rather than a primary mechanistic predictor.
limitations: Likely proxy for regional climate and snow/oceanicity; weak direct mechanism.

biological_hypothesis: High light can induce petal anthocyanin and increase photoprotective value, especially under co-stress.
public_proxy: CHELSA RSDS mean; terrain-informed 30 arc-sec climatology
evidence: UV-B and light induce anthocyanin biosynthesis in petals; current dryness x RSDS state interaction is suggestive but not transfer-robust.
limitations: Total shortwave radiation, not UV-B or flower-level illumination.

biological_hypothesis: UV-B can directly induce petal anthocyanin.
limitations: Coarse spatial resolution and period mismatch relative to the 1-km 2023-2025 study; use RSDS claim ceiling.

candidate: Soil PC1 (organic matter/N/bulk density/pH) and PC2 (texture)
biological_hypothesis: Nutrient/resource status, pH, texture and water retention can constrain pigment biosynthesis and drought response.
public_proxy: SoilGrids 2.0 0-5 cm properties at 250 m aggregated to the common grid
evidence: Anthocyanin pathways respond to resource and drought context; SoilGrids provides harmonized N, C, pH, bulk density and texture.
limitations: No phosphorus/potassium axis; prediction uncertainty; topsoil may not represent rhizosphere depth.

biological_hypothesis: Terrain relief generates heterogeneous drainage and microclimatic context, but is not a single stress direction.
public_proxy: WorldClim elevation-derived slope, TRI and roughness
evidence: Current data show a negative additive association with conditional intensity; temperature x terrain failed geographic transfer.
key_sources: current exact INLA-SPDE audit; WorldClim 2.1 documentation
limitations: Does not directly measure aspect, canopy, hydrology, snow or flower-level light.

biological_hypothesis: Canopy/open-habitat context can alter petal-development light and image illumination.
public_proxy: MLIT 2021 forest fraction at 1-km exact sites
evidence: Light regulates petal anthocyanin; C. punctata occurs in bright grassland/forest-edge habitats.
limitations: Forest fraction is not canopy closure at the photographed flower and may also reflect human land use.

biological_hypothesis: Coastality may proxy maritime thermal regime, salt/wind exposure, habitat forms and island history.
public_proxy: Distance from WorldClim land mask to nearest sea cell
evidence: C. punctata and var. hondoensis span coastal-to-subalpine habitats; island populations are genetically differentiated.
limitations: Composite geographical proxy and strongly spatial; not direct salt or wind exposure.

biological_hypothesis: Flower age/phenology and year-specific conditions could affect visible colour or sampling composition.
public_proxy: Complete photo date, DOY, 2023-2025 year indicators
evidence: Environmental regulation of floral anthocyanin can operate during flower development; current climate normals cannot identify plasticity.
limitations: DOY is partly an outcome of geography/phenology; year indicators are not weather measurements.

biological_hypothesis: Spatial patterns should persist after basic image-formation diagnostics are controlled.
evidence: Community-photo colour includes illumination and camera variation; current QC flags were not used to response-select records.
limitations: Diagnostics do not calibrate white balance, reflectance or UV.

biological_hypothesis: Separates plastic colour response from long-term regional differentiation.
evidence: Floral anthocyanin is developmentally temperature/light/drought responsive.
limitations: Requires a new time-varying acquisition and pre-anthesis-window design; should not be mixed post hoc into the current long-term biogeographic model.

candidate: var. punctata versus var. hondoensis / coastal forms
biological_hypothesis: Taxonomic or lineage mixture may generate regional colour and spatial-field structure.
public_proxy: Requires image-level calyx morphology audit or genetic/taxonomic data; no defensible raster proxy
evidence: var. hondoensis is morphologically recognized and spans coastal-to-subalpine central Japan; the current image table lacks variety identity.
limitations: Geographic proxying would be circular and misclassify overlap.
